title: Add KV cache telemetry v2 dashboards (hit-rate, hit-bytes, saved-prefill-ms) + regression alert templates
author: Sergio Costa
description: Summary: Adds the first set of dashboard JSONs and alert templates for KV/prefix cache telemetry v2. Dashboards cover cache hit-rate (including outcome breakdown), hit-bytes, saved prefill time (saved_prefill_ms), and a cacheable prompt ratio view. Includes drilldowns by deployment_mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), region, route, model, and (safely) tenant. Also adds regression alert templates intended to be instantiated by SRE per env/tier. Motivation: We have runtime + gateway work landing v2 cache telemetry; we need dashboards that are (a) consistent with the v2 metric spec, (b) usable during staged rollout, and (c) resilient to sampling and cardinality guardrails. This PR is the observability-pack side only (no runtime changes). Key details: Panels use the v2 aggregated fields (no request_id; no raw prefix hashes). Queries are written to prefer low-cardinality groupings: route_id (stable), model_family/model_id (not full model_version by default), and region/deployment_mode. A separate "high-cardinality drilldown" dashboard is included but gated behind a template variable that defaults to OFF and warns about cost. saved_prefill_ms is displayed as both total saved ms and saved ms per 1k requests; we explicitly annotate that it’s an estimate and depends on partial-prefill accounting. Alerts: (1) Cache hit-rate regression alert template (burn-rate style) scoped to {deployment_mode, region} with optional route_id grouping, using a 30m/6h pair and minimum request volume guard. (2) saved_prefill_ms regression template (ratio-based) to catch cases where hit-rate is stable but savings drop (often indicates misclassification/partial-prefill bug or prompt mix change). Both templates include noise controls: request floor, suppression window during rollouts, and a "traffic mix changed" runbook link placeholder. Rollout: Intended to be merged ahead of the broad telemetry enablement. Dashboards rely on metric existence checks so they don’t hard-fail when v2 is off in a region; panels display "No data" rather than broken queries. Notes/Assumptions: Metric names/tags follow kv-cache-telemetry-v2 spec as of 2025-02-20: outcomes are cache_outcome in {hit, miss, partial}; rollup metrics are emitted at 1m resolution with sampling_rate tag. We do not group by model_version by default to avoid cardinality blowups during canaries; version drilldown is available in a separate view. Testing: Ran dashboard validation (schema + query lint), imported dashboards into staging Datadog, verified queries against synthetic fixtures from ENG-4815 backfill dataset (Mei’s staging dataset). Screenshots attached in internal PR comment (not included here). Release notes: Adds new dashboards under "Inference Runtime -> Cache (v2)" and new alert templates under "SRE -> Cache -> KV cache telemetry v2".

review_conversation: Allison Grant: Please ensure all group-bys default to the approved cardinality budget (no model_version or tenant_id by default). Also add an explicit note about the high-cardinality drilldown dashboard and how to use it safely.

Sergio Costa (author): Done. Defaults now group by {deployment_mode, region} and optionally route_id. model_version is only available via an opt-in template var on the drilldown dashboard. Added warnings + README section on cost and tag explosion symptoms.

Logan Wright: Metric names in the hit-rate formula should use the v2 aggregation metric, not raw lookup events. In particular, use cache_outcome counts from ri.cache.lookup.count (aggregated) so sampling is handled consistently. Also, please add a panel for partial rate (partial / (hit+miss+partial)) to catch misclassification during rollout.

Sergio Costa (author): Updated to use the aggregated counter and sampling-normalized query fragment. Added "Partial outcome ratio" panel and linked it to the known-issues runbook placeholder. Also updated the annotations to clarify partial-prefill behavior.
Rafael Mendes: Alert templates: can we avoid paging on hit-rate changes when traffic is low or when a region is mid-rollout? We got burned by that on prior telemetry rollouts.

Sergio Costa (author): Added minimum request volume guard (default 2k req/30m) and a rollout suppression tag (rollout_stage=canary) that can be set by the pipeline. Template defaults to page only at rollout_stage=stable; can be overridden per env.

Mei Lin: Dashboard backfill: please keep the time series names stable; we’ll use them in the backfill validation notebook. Also the cacheable_prompt_ratio panel should compute off the v2 eligible counter rather than inferred from total requests.

Sergio Costa (author): Renamed the series to stable identifiers and switched cacheable_prompt_ratio to eligible_count / request_count using the v2 eligible metric. Added a note that eligible_count excludes streaming-retry replays per the spec.
Thomas Baird: Query cost: the high-cardinality drilldown dashboard should hard-cap series count (top N) and default to a short time range.
Sergio Costa (author): Implemented top(50) cap on route_id/model_id breakdowns and set the default time range to last 4 hours in the dashboard JSON. README updated with rationale.
Allison Grant: Approved once the README includes the tag set and the explicit anti-pattern list (request_id, full prompt hash, arbitrary customer_id).
Sergio Costa (author): Added anti-pattern list + linked to the telemetry spec section on tag budgets.
Rafael Mendes: Approved (please coordinate actual alert enabling in ENG-4817 rollout checklist).
merge_summary: Merged to main after approvals; alert templates not enabled by default (SRE will instantiate per region/tier during rollout).
release_notes: New: KV cache telemetry v2 dashboards (hit-rate, hit-bytes, saved_prefill_ms, cacheable prompt ratio) and regression alert templates with noise controls and rollout suppression support.
